Area.evidence_source: The sense of liberation and of a solution to unsolvable problems or to unbearable pain was commonly considered the main reason for attempting suicide: [page/3/Text/11] The existence of a psychiatric disorder was unanimously considered an important contributing factor to the origin of suicidal ideas and attempts; in particular alcoholism (generally considered a self-therapy element and, at the same time, a facilitating factor in the emergence of suicidal impulses), depression (even when part of a bipolar disorder) and auditory hallucinations: [page/3/Text/19] The decision was made in an isolated and secretive manner and was characterized by exclusiveness. Suicidal thoughts were not communicated to relatives, friends or health care providers: [page/3/Text/27]
